articles.title: WCS manual flush procedure during low-gravity transit
articles.body:
## Procedure

1. Verify WCS panel C3 shows PRESS FAULT indicator illuminated.
2. Close inlet valve WCS-V-101 (quarter turn clockwise).
3. Engage manual flush pump via switch panel D2, position 3.
4. Monitor pressure gauge WCS-PG-04 for stabilization (nominal: 12–15 psi).
5. If pressure stabilizes, open inlet valve slowly (quarter turn counter-clockwise).
6. If pressure does not stabilize within 60 seconds, proceed to WCS backup bag system (stowage locker L4-B).

## Notes
- During low-gravity coast phases, air-liquid separation in the WCS is less reliable. Extended flush cycles (45s vs standard 30s) may be required.
- Always don clean gloves from WCS maintenance kit before servicing.

## Applicable Missions
All crewed Orion missions (Artemis II+)

## References
- Orion Crew Operations Manual, Section 7.4.2
- WCS Vendor Maintenance Guide Rev. C

articles.title: CO2 scrubber cartridge replacement procedure
articles.body:
## Overview
The Orion ECLSS uses lithium hydroxide (LiOH) cartridges for CO2 removal. Standard replacement interval is 24 hours under nominal crew metabolic load.

## Procedure
1. Retrieve fresh cartridge from stowage location E2-A (vacuum-sealed).
2. Power down scrubber fan assembly via ECLSS panel A1, switch 4.
3. Wait 30 seconds for fan spindown.
4. Release used cartridge latches (2x quarter-turn).
5. Slide used cartridge out, insert fresh cartridge until latches click.
6. Power up scrubber fan assembly.
7. Verify CO2 ppm on environmental display returns to nominal (<5000 ppm) within 15 minutes.
8. Bag used cartridge and stow in waste container W3.

## Emergency Notes
If CO2 exceeds 15,000 ppm before replacement is complete, don emergency O2 masks from panel F1.

articles.title: S-band emergency communications fallback
articles.body:
## When to Use
If primary Ka-band link is lost and cannot be re-established within 10 minutes, switch to S-band emergency communications.

## Procedure
1. On COMM panel B2, switch MODE selector from KA-PRIMARY to S-BAND.
2. Set S-band power to HIGH (switch B2-7).
3. Verify signal acquisition on TDRS status display.
4. Notify ground via S-band voice: 'Houston, [callsign], S-band emergency comm active.'
5. S-band provides voice and low-rate telemetry only. No video capability.

## TDRS Coverage
S-band coverage via TDRS is not continuous. Expect comm blackouts of up to 20 minutes during certain orbital positions. Crew should pre-compose critical messages for burst transmission during coverage windows.

## Return to Ka-band
Attempt Ka-band re-acquisition every 30 minutes. If Ka-band is restored, switch back and confirm with Houston.

articles.title: Solar array gimbal troubleshooting
articles.body:
## Symptoms
- Solar array power output below expected levels
- Gimbal position telemetry shows fixed angle despite sun tracking commands
- Array temperature asymmetry between panels

## Diagnostic Steps
1. Check gimbal motor current on POWER panel P3 display.
2. If motor current is zero: suspect motor driver failure. Switch to backup driver via P3 switch 9.
3. If motor current is nominal but gimbal not moving: suspect mechanical binding. Request ground control analysis of thermal expansion data.
4. If backup driver also shows zero current: gimbal is offline. Reconfigure power budget for single-wing operation.

## Power Budget Impact
Single-wing operation provides approximately 60% of nominal power. Non-essential loads must be shed per POWER-CONTINGENCY-001 checklist.

articles.title: EVA suit pressurization pre-check
articles.body:
## Pre-EVA Checklist
1. Begin suit pressurization 90 minutes before planned EVA start.
2. Set suit pressure to 4.3 psi (29.6 kPa) for standard EVA.
3. Verify O2 flow rate on suit display: nominal 6.0 L/min.
4. Check suit integrity: pressure drop must not exceed 0.1 psi over 5-minute hold.
5. Verify CO2 sensor reads <1000 ppm.
6. Check cooling water loop temperature: 50–60°F (10–15°C).
7. Confirm helmet camera and lights functional.
8. Verify comm check with CAPCOM on EVA frequency.

## Abort Criteria
- Pressure drop >0.3 psi during hold test
- O2 flow rate outside 4.5–7.5 L/min range
- Any visible damage to suit outer layer
- Cooling loop temperature outside 40–70°F range

articles.title: Crew exercise protocol — cardiovascular and resistive
articles.body:
## Daily Requirements
Each crew member must complete 2.5 hours of exercise per day to mitigate bone density loss and muscle atrophy:
- 1 hour cardiovascular (CEVIS cycle ergometer or T2 treadmill)
- 1.5 hours resistive (ARED device)

## CEVIS Cycle Ergometer
- Located in middeck, position M4
- Standard protocol: 30 min warmup at 75W, 20 min intervals (150W/75W), 10 min cooldown
- Heart rate monitoring via chest strap required

## ARED (Advanced Resistive Exercise Device)
- Located in middeck, position M6
- Protocol includes: squats, deadlifts, heel raises, bench press, shoulder press
- Vacuum cylinders provide up to 600 lbs resistance

## Logging
All exercise sessions must be logged in crew health system with duration, type, and peak heart rate.

articles.title: Orion star tracker calibration procedure
articles.body:
## Overview
The Orion navigation system uses two star trackers for attitude determination. Calibration drift may occur after significant thermal transients (e.g., exiting Earth shadow, lunar orbit insertion).

## Calibration Procedure
1. Place vehicle in free-drift attitude hold.
2. On NAV panel N1, select STAR TRACKER > CALIBRATE.
3. System will acquire 3+ reference stars (takes 2–5 minutes).
4. Verify attitude solution convergence: residual should be <0.05 degrees.
5. If residual exceeds 0.05 degrees, repeat with vehicle in different attitude.
6. Log calibration results for ground analysis.

## When to Calibrate
- After any eclipse exit >45 minutes
- After RCS maneuvers >5 m/s delta-V
- If navigation display shows ATTITUDE DEGRADED warning
- Every 12 hours as routine maintenance

articles.title: Thermal control system — radiator bypass valve operation
articles.body:
## Purpose
The active thermal control system (ATCS) uses external radiators to reject waste heat. Bypass valves route coolant around radiators when heat rejection must be reduced (e.g., cold case attitude, eclipse periods).

## Manual Override
1. On THERMAL panel T2, select RADIATOR > BYPASS.
2. Set bypass percentage (0% = full radiator flow, 100% = full bypass).
3. Monitor cabin temperature response. Adjustment lag is approximately 15 minutes.
4. Target cabin temperature: 65–78°F (18–26°C).

## Caution
- Never set bypass to 100% for more than 2 hours — equipment overheating risk.
- If cabin temp exceeds 85°F, return bypass to 0% and notify ground control.
- Radiator ice formation may occur below -40°F external. Ground control monitors this.

articles.title: Water quality testing and purification
articles.body:
## Routine Testing
Crew must test potable water supply every 48 hours using the Water Quality Monitor (WQM) in galley position G2.

## Parameters
- Total organic carbon (TOC): <3.0 mg/L
- pH: 6.0–8.5
- Turbidity: <1.0 NTU
- Free chlorine residual: 0.2–0.5 mg/L

## If Parameters Out of Range
1. Switch to backup water supply (tank B, valve G2-V-03).
2. Add chlorine tablet to primary tank (dosing: 1 tablet per 10L).
3. Wait 2 hours, retest.
4. If still out of range, report to ground control for further analysis.

## Emergency Water
Emergency water pouches (72hr supply for 4 crew) located in stowage locker E1-C.

articles.title: RCS thruster manual firing procedure
articles.body:
## When to Use
Manual RCS firing is authorized only when automated attitude control is unavailable and vehicle attitude is diverging beyond safe limits.

## Procedure
1. On PROP panel R1, switch RCS MODE from AUTO to MANUAL.
2. Use rotational hand controller (RHC) for attitude corrections.
3. Minimum pulse: 0.1 seconds. Maximum continuous burn: 5 seconds.
4. Monitor propellant remaining on R1 display.
5. Once attitude is stabilized, return RCS MODE to AUTO.
6. Report all manual firings to ground control with timestamp, axis, and duration.

## Propellant Budget
Orion carries 1,740 lbs of MMH/NTO for RCS. Manual firings consume approximately 0.5 lbs per second. Excessive manual firing may jeopardize mission propellant reserves.

articles.title: Cabin pressure leak detection and response
articles.body:
## Detection
Cabin pressure is monitored continuously. If pressure drops below 14.2 psi (from nominal 14.7 psi), CABIN PRESS LOW alarm will sound.

## Immediate Response
1. Don O2 masks from emergency stations (4 stations: F1, F2, F3, F4).
2. Verify pressure drop rate on ECLSS panel A1.
3. If drop rate >0.1 psi/min: this is a rapid leak. Proceed to leak isolation.
4. If drop rate <0.1 psi/min: slow leak. Begin systematic compartment isolation.

## Leak Isolation
1. Close all inter-module hatches.
2. Monitor pressure in each compartment independently.
3. Compartment with continuing drop contains the leak.
4. Use ultrasonic leak detector from repair kit R2 to localize.
5. Apply emergency patch from repair kit R2.

## Critical
If cabin pressure reaches 10.2 psi, initiate emergency suit donning and prepare for potential abort.

articles.title: Crew meal preparation and schedule
articles.body:
## Meal Schedule
- Breakfast: MET +0:30 after wake
- Lunch: MET +6:00 after wake
- Dinner: MET +12:00 after wake
- Snacks available ad libitum from snack locker G1-B

## Preparation
Most meals are thermostabilized or freeze-dried.
- Thermostabilized: open pouch, insert in food warmer (position G3) for 10 minutes.
- Freeze-dried: inject hot water via rehydration port. Wait 5 minutes.
- Beverages: rehydrate powder in drink pouch. Shake well.

## Rotation
Meal rotation follows a 10-day cycle. Current cycle and menu posted on galley display. Crew may trade meals with mutual consent.

## Waste
All food packaging goes in wet waste container W1. Minimize crumbs — they become FOD in microgravity.

articles.title: Docking procedure — Orion to Gateway HALO module
articles.body:
## Prerequisites
- Vehicle within 200m of Gateway station
- LIDAR docking sensor active (NAV panel N2)
- RCS in AUTO mode with sufficient propellant (>500 lbs)
- Docking port alignment confirmed by ground control

## Procedure
1. Begin approach at 0.3 m/s closure rate.
2. At 50m, reduce to 0.1 m/s.
3. At 10m, switch to FINE APPROACH mode on NAV panel.
4. LIDAR guides final alignment. Crew monitors cross-hair display.
5. Contact and capture confirmed by DOCK CAPTURED indicator.
6. Initiate hard dock: DOCK panel D1, press HARD DOCK.
7. Wait for 12 latches to engage (green indicators on D1).
8. Verify pressure seal: equalize pressure between Orion and HALO.
9. Open hatch only after pressure equalization confirmed.

## Abort
At any point before capture, crew can press ABORT on DOCK panel for automated retreat to 200m safe distance.

articles.title: Radiation exposure monitoring and storm shelter protocol
articles.body:
## Monitoring
Each crew member wears a personal radiation dosimeter (PRD). Real-time dose rate displayed on MED panel M1.
- Nominal dose rate in cislunar space: 0.5–1.0 mSv/day
- During solar particle event (SPE): can exceed 50 mSv/hour

## SPE Warning
Ground control issues SPE warnings based on solar observatory data. Warning time is typically 30–60 minutes before particle arrival.

## Storm Shelter Procedure
1. On SPE WARNING alarm, all crew proceed to storm shelter (middeck center, behind water wall stowage).
2. Configure water wall panels around shelter area per diagram SHELTER-01.
3. Remain in shelter until ground control issues ALL CLEAR.
4. Log individual dosimeter readings before and after event.

## Dose Limits
- 30-day limit: 250 mSv
- Annual limit: 500 mSv
- Career limit: varies by age and sex (see NASA-STD-3001)

articles.title: O2 generation system — electrolysis unit operation
articles.body:
## Overview
The OGS (Oxygen Generation System) electrolyzes water to produce O2 and H2. The H2 is vented overboard.

## Nominal Operation
- OGS runs continuously in AUTO mode
- O2 production rate: 5.4 kg/day (supports 4 crew)
- Water consumption: 6.8 kg/day
- Power consumption: 1.4 kW

## Manual Start
If OGS is offline and AUTO restart fails:
1. On ECLSS panel A2, verify water supply valve is OPEN.
2. Set OGS MODE to MANUAL.
3. Press OGS START. Unit takes 10 minutes to reach steady state.
4. Verify O2 output on ECLSS display.

## Backup
If OGS cannot be restarted, switch to backup O2 from high-pressure tanks (ECLSS panel A2, O2 BACKUP switch). Backup supply: 72 hours for 4 crew.

articles.title: Emergency O2 mask usage
articles.body:
## Location
Emergency O2 masks at 4 stations: F1 (forward), F2 (mid-port), F3 (mid-starboard), F4 (aft).

## Usage
1. Pull mask from housing (breaks seal).
2. Place over nose and mouth.
3. Tighten straps.
4. Breathe normally — O2 flow starts automatically on seal break.
5. Supply duration: 15 minutes per mask.

## When to Use
- CABIN PRESS LOW alarm
- CO2 >15,000 ppm
- Smoke or fire detection
- Any atmosphere contamination warning

articles.title: Stowage map and inventory system
articles.body:
## System
All stowage locations are tracked in the Inventory Management System (IMS) on the crew laptop. Search by item name, barcode, or location code.

## Location Codes
Format: [Module][Deck]-[Bay][Shelf]
- Module: F=Forward, M=Mid, A=Aft
- Deck: 1=Upper, 2=Lower
- Bay: A–F (port to starboard)
- Shelf: 1–4 (top to bottom)

Example: M2-C3 = Middeck, lower, bay C, shelf 3

## Crew Responsibility
After using any item, scan barcode and return to assigned location. Items found adrift must be scanned and re-stowed. Stowage discipline prevents FOD and enables emergency access to critical items.

articles.title: Toilet troubleshooting — WCS pressure issues in microgravity
articles.body:
## Common Issues
The Waste Collection System can experience pressure faults in microgravity due to air/liquid separation challenges.

## Quick Fix
1. Turn off WCS via panel C3.
2. Wait 30 seconds.
3. Turn WCS back on.
4. If fault clears, resume normal use.

## If Fault Persists
Follow the manual flush procedure. Close the inlet valve, run the manual pump, and check if pressure normalizes. If not, switch to backup bags.

## Tips
- Extended flush cycles help in low-g.
- Keep the area clean to prevent sensor fouling.

articles.title: Lunar south pole EVA surface operations
articles.body:
## Overview
Artemis III and subsequent missions include lunar surface EVAs at the south pole. Conditions differ significantly from orbital EVA.

## Key Differences from Orbital EVA
- Gravity: 1/6 g — mobility is possible but suit mass still applies
- Dust: lunar regolith is highly abrasive and electrostatically charged
- Lighting: near-permanent shadow in craters, extreme contrast at terminator
- Temperature: -230°C in shadow, +120°C in sunlight

## Surface EVA Protocol
1. Complete standard suit pressurization pre-check (see KB-005).
2. Deploy dust mitigation: brush suits before re-entry, use dust-tolerant seals.
3. Maximum EVA duration: 6.5 hours.
4. Maintain line-of-sight or relay comm with lander at all times.
5. Sample collection: use numbered bags, photograph each sample location.

articles.title: MMOD impact assessment procedure
articles.body:
## Detection
Micrometeoroid and Orbital Debris (MMOD) impacts may be detected by:
- Cabin pressure sensors (slow leak)
- Audible impact sound
- Visual inspection during EVA

## Assessment
1. If cabin pressure stable: note time and approximate location of sound/sensor alert.
2. If pressure dropping: see KB-011 (Cabin pressure leak detection).
3. Schedule visual inspection of suspected impact area during next EVA or via external cameras.
4. Report to ground control with: time, location estimate, pressure data, any visible damage.

## Risk Areas
Highest MMOD risk areas on Orion: forward heat shield seams, solar array blankets, radiator panels. Whipple shielding protects crew module walls.

articles.title: Crew sleep station configuration
articles.body:
## Locations
Four sleep stations in crew module: S1 (port-forward), S2 (port-aft), S3 (starboard-forward), S4 (starboard-aft).

## Configuration
- Sleeping bag attaches to wall via Velcro strips
- Light shield for each station
- Personal ventilation fan (adjust via station control panel)
- Ear protection available in personal kit

## Schedule
Crew sleep period: 8 hours. Staggered if mission requires continuous operations. Quiet hours apply to all crew during any crew member's sleep period.

## Sleep Disruption Reporting
If sleep quality is poor for >2 consecutive nights, report to Flight Surgeon via private medical conference.

articles.title: Ka-band high-gain antenna pointing procedure
articles.body:
## When Needed
Ka-band antenna must be manually pointed when auto-tracking fails or after vehicle attitude change >15 degrees.

## Procedure
1. On COMM panel B2, select KA-BAND > MANUAL POINT.
2. Use TDRS ephemeris data (displayed on COMM screen) to determine target azimuth/elevation.
3. Adjust antenna via B2 joystick. Signal strength meter shows real-time feedback.
4. When signal strength exceeds -80 dBm, press LOCK to engage auto-track from current position.
5. Verify data rate indicator shows HIGH (16 Mbps downlink).

## Troubleshooting
If signal cannot be acquired within 5 minutes, TDRS may be below horizon. Check TDRS visibility schedule on COMM screen and wait for next window, or switch to S-band (see KB-003).

articles.title: Fire detection and suppression
articles.body:
## Detection
Smoke detectors in all modules. FIRE alarm on master alarm panel with location indicator.

## Response
1. Don O2 masks (nearest station F1–F4).
2. Locate fire using indicator panel and visual/smell.
3. If small and accessible: use portable fire extinguisher (CO2, location: each module has 2, marked with red stripe).
4. If not containable: isolate module by closing hatches, cut power to affected area via circuit breaker panel.
5. Report to ground control immediately.

## Post-Fire
- Do not remove O2 masks until atmosphere is tested for toxic gases.
- Ground control will advise on atmosphere scrubbing duration.
- Document all damage for structural assessment.

articles.title: Pharmaceutical inventory and dispensing
articles.body:
## Overview
The onboard pharmacy contains medications for common conditions encountered during long-duration spaceflight.

## Access
Pharmacy locker: M1-D2 (requires crew medical officer access code).

## Common Medications
- Space motion sickness: promethazine (IM injection or suppository)
- Headache/pain: acetaminophen, ibuprofen
- Nasal congestion (common in microgravity): pseudoephedrine, saline spray
- Sleep aid: zolpidem (Flight Surgeon approval required)
- Skin irritation: hydrocortisone cream

## Protocol
All medication dispensing must be logged in crew health system with: crew member, medication, dose, time, reason. Flight Surgeon must approve sleep aids and antibiotics via private medical conference.

## Expiration
Check expiration dates monthly. Expired medications go in pharma waste container in locker M1-D3.

articles.title: Abort modes and decision criteria
articles.body:
## Abort Modes by Mission Phase

### Launch to Orbit
- **Mode I (Pad Abort)**: LAS fires, capsule separates. T-0 to T+2:30.
- **Mode II (Ascent Abort)**: LAS fires during ascent. T+2:30 to LAS jettison.
- **Mode III (Orbit Insertion Abort)**: OMS burn to safe orbit or direct entry.

### Translunar
- **Free Return**: No burn required. Gravity returns vehicle to Earth. +3 days.
- **Powered Return**: OMS burn to shorten return. Used if crew health emergency.

### Lunar Orbit
- **TEI Abort**: Trans-Earth injection burn from lunar orbit. Standard return.
- **Contingency TEI**: Backup burn profile if primary OMS fails.

## Decision Authority
- Launch aborts: automated or Flight Director call
- In-flight aborts: Flight Director with crew commander concurrence
- Medical aborts: Flight Surgeon recommendation to Flight Director

articles.title: WCS waste collection in reduced gravity — tips and best practices
articles.body:
## General Tips
The WCS (Waste Collection System) works differently in reduced gravity compared to ground training.

- Positioning is key. Use the foot restraints and thigh bars.
- The airflow is what directs waste. Make sure the fan is running before use.
- For liquid waste, the funnel adapter with hose provides better results than direct collection.
- In microgravity, the standard flush time of 30 seconds is often not enough. Try 45 seconds.

## Common Complaints
- 'It doesn't flush properly' — usually an airflow issue. Check fan and inlet valve.
- 'Pressure fault keeps coming back' — likely debris in the pressure relief valve. See maintenance procedure.

## Cleaning
Clean WCS surfaces after each use with disinfectant wipes from hygiene kit H1. Weekly deep clean per schedule.

articles.title: Battery thermal runaway emergency procedure
articles.body:
## Detection
- Battery management system (BMS) alarm on POWER panel P1
- Rapid temperature rise (>5°C/min) on battery module
- Possible acrid smell

## Immediate Actions
1. Disconnect affected battery bank: POWER panel P1, circuit breaker for indicated bank.
2. Don O2 masks if any smell detected.
3. Monitor adjacent battery banks for thermal contagion.
4. If temperature stabilizes: continue monitoring for 2 hours.
5. If temperature continues rising: vent module atmosphere per ground control direction.

## Prevention
- Battery charge limited to 90% during coast phases to reduce thermal stress
- Ground control monitors all battery temperatures continuously

articles.title: Photo documentation requirements
articles.body:
## Required Documentation
Crew must photograph:
- All anomalies and damage (minimum 3 angles)
- Daily vehicle inspection results
- EVA worksite before and after
- Sample collection locations (lunar surface)
- Stowage configuration changes

## Camera Equipment
- Nikon Z9 (2x) — stowage M2-A1
- GoPro (4x) — EVA helmet mount and worksite
- iPad for quick documentation

## File Management
All photos must be tagged with: date, time, crew member, category, description. Upload to ground via Ka-band during scheduled data dump windows.

## Public Affairs
NASA PAO may request specific crew photos for public engagement. These requests come via CAPCOM and are always optional.

articles.title: Orion service module jettison checklist
articles.body:
## Pre-Jettison (T-30 min)
1. Verify all service module consumables transferred or accounted for.
2. Close SM-to-CM fluid umbilicals (automated, verify on PROP panel).
3. Retract solar arrays (POWER panel P2).
4. Configure CM for independent power and thermal.

## Jettison (T-0)
1. Flight Director GO/NO-GO poll.
2. Arm separation pyros: SM SEP panel, ARM switch (guarded).
3. On Flight Director call: press SM SEP FIRE.
4. Verify separation on DOCK panel indicators (4 green = clean sep).
5. CM performs small RCS burn to increase separation distance.

## Post-Jettison
- Confirm heat shield exposure and alignment for entry
- Begin entry checklist
- SM will burn up on reentry — no recovery

articles.title: WCS maintenance and cleaning procedures
articles.body:
## Routine Maintenance (Weekly)
1. Inspect WCS fan and inlet screen for debris.
2. Clean all surfaces with disinfectant.
3. Check pressure relief valve (WCS-PRV-03) for blockage.
4. Verify seal integrity on waste canisters.
5. Log maintenance in IMS.

## Pressure Relief Valve Cleaning
If pressure faults are recurring:
1. Close inlet valve WCS-V-101.
2. Remove PRV-03 (quarter turn, pull straight out).
3. Inspect for debris. Clean with alcohol wipe.
4. Reinstall PRV-03. Verify seated with light push.
5. Open inlet valve. Run test flush.

## Consumables
- WCS bags (backup): stowage L4-B, qty 40
- Disinfectant wipes: hygiene kit H1
- PRV cleaning kit: repair kit R1

## Notes
Extended flush cycles (45s) recommended in microgravity. Standard 30s often insufficient.
